Javier Godoy — Staff Software Engineer

"A king without scars is not a King."

New York, NY · gaulatti.com · LinkedIn · jack@gaulatti.com

About Me

Staff Software Engineer with 15+ years of experience building production systems across healthcare, fintech, media, and e-commerce. My work spans AI infrastructure, developer platforms, distributed systems, and real-time production.

Currently at Medsender, building an LLM Gateway, MCP services, developer tooling, and engineering automation. Previously at Amazon, Warner Bros. Discovery (CNN), and Narmi.

Outside work, I independently design, build, and operate software for newsrooms, broadcasting, and photography, using my own resources. I've completed all academic requirements for the WGU B.S. in Software Engineering; degree conferral is pending. Recently earned CompTIA Project+.

Experience

Period Company Role
Jul 2026 – Present Medsender Staff Software Engineer
Jun 2025 – Mar 2026 Narmi Software Engineer
Jan 2023 – May 2025 Warner Bros. Discovery (CNN) Staff Software Engineer
Feb 2017 – Jan 2023 Amazon Software Development Engineer

Highlights

Medsender (Jul 2026 – Present)

  • AI Infrastructure — Launched a customer-facing LLM Gateway for production AI workflows and build MCP services to connect tools and systems.
  • Developer Platforms — Own the developer portal and build AI-assisted review and governance tooling, engineering automation, and deployment safeguards.

Narmi (Jun 2025 – Mar 2026)
Created the original version of AI DecisionAssist, using Anthropic Claude via Amazon Bedrock to turn identity-verification data into risk assessments and actionable recommendations for account-opening reviewers. Mentored a junior engineer to lead tactical execution while guiding integration strategy and technical direction.

Warner Bros. Discovery / CNN (Jan 2023 – May 2025)

  • Design Systems — Delivered CNN's design system internally with two engineers in seven months, avoiding a planned $3M agency engagement. Built an automated Figma-to-code pipeline using TypeScript, NestJS, and Style Dictionary.
  • Site Performance — Built a performance-observability platform combining real-user metrics, Lighthouse CI, and PageSpeed Insights. Drove adoption across Live Story and Politics ahead of the 2024 election and identified livestreaming components as a major performance bottleneck.

Amazon (Feb 2017 – Jan 2023)

  • Amazon Explore — Owned the defect-reduction program, reducing catastrophic session failures from 40% to 1.3% over six months and clearing the executive launch gate. Built observability using AWS IoT Core and CloudWatch and traced failures across Redux Saga and WebRTC.
  • Alexa Shopping — Led peak-event readiness across 15 global teams and improved monitoring after uncovering a silent production outage.
  • Payments — Launched EBT and HSA/FSA payment support, including eligibility verification, tax allocation, and multi-tender purchase flows.

ModoItaliano — Sanremo Festival (Feb 2026)

In February 2026, led technical production and live operations for Sanremo Festival coverage with ModoItaliano, fifthbell, and HNMag across three countries. When the original setup failed, rebuilt the broadcast architecture in approximately three days and ran multi-hour broadcasts with distributed contributors.

Projects

I designed and built these projects independently, using my own resources. Each link opens its architecture, engineering decisions, evidence, and available source or application links.

Project Description Stack
Mistify A shared AI service for language detection, translation, classification, clustering, and recorded-media analysis. Python, FastAPI, gRPC, PyTorch, Redis
Colombo A Rust upload gateway that accepts photographs over FTP, FTPS, and HTTP, then delivers them to storage and a newsroom CMS. Rust, FTP/FTPS, HTTP, AWS S3, PostgreSQL
Guggiana An article-to-audio pipeline coordinating translation, speech synthesis, reusable language renditions, and audio assembly. AWS Step Functions, Polly, DynamoDB, Python, TypeScript
Monitor A workspace for following developing stories, grouping related coverage, and tracking events across multiple feeds. Rust, React, PostgreSQL, pgvector
Pompeii A shared authentication and authorization service for application permissions, feature flags, and identity management. Go, APIs, Authorization, Feature flags
Bleecker A React component library with shared typography, design tokens, accessible controls, and application layouts. React, TypeScript, Design tokens, Accessibility, Storybook
Alcántara A broadcast control surface for graphics, program state, media, and live guest contributions. React, NestJS, PostgreSQL, SSE, WebRTC
Alana A headless runtime that renders an Alcántara program and publishes independent RTMP outputs and an optional low-latency feed. Python, Chromium, FFmpeg, RTMP, LiveKit
Croccante An RTMP relay with independently supervised destinations, explicit broadcast lifecycle control, and prepared continuity media. Python, nginx-rtmp, FFmpeg, RTMP
Palazzo A self-hosted radio controller combining a NestJS API with Liquidsoap and Icecast. NestJS, Liquidsoap, Icecast, SSE
Broadway A template editor with generated forms, live preview, and high-quality image and document exports. React Router, TypeScript, PNG, Vector PDF
Cronkite A CMS-directed rendering service that turns approved content and presentation manifests into authorized publishing artifacts. TypeScript, AWS S3, FFmpeg
Celesti A channel inventory and display-management platform with service-controlled playback clients. Go, Kotlin, Jetpack Compose, SSE

Hi there 👋 I'm Ralph

I'm a freelance product engineer, always working on a wide variety of projects. Over time, I have worked for many clients, each having their own interesting environment and constraints, ranging from small-scale startups to large enterprises.

I started out building websites and themes. Over the years my work moved to Laravel, Filament and Livewire, developing an eye for interface design and motion along the way. Lately with AI, more of my time goes to architecture and quality, broadening myself across the stack.

Next to client work, I run Filament Plugins. I sell eight premium plugins there, including Filament Media Library Pro, Filament Activitylog Pro and Filament Upload Pro, and build and support each of them myself, crossing over 1.25M installs recently. I am a top-5 contributor to Filament and maintain several open-source packages of my own. Furthermore, I also run a popular newsletter called Filament Biweekly.

Recently I also graduated with an MSc Information Management, complementing my experience as a software developer.
